read_scope: native test names and lifetime controls

findings.detail: Unix current-user peer check occurs before permit acquisition. Windows pending connections have no application I/O path until authenticate succeeds; authentication and normal handling share the original two-second timeout. Owned permit is retained by the spawned task and drops on timeout, error, completion or task cancellation.

No-permit Windows connections authenticate before receiving the constant overload frame. Authentication/write/shutdown share the original 50 ms bound. This can serialize overload processing for that bounded period; it does not permit unauthenticated application frames.

ControlStream alias changes transport. Existing bounded newline frame, request ID, expected AgentId and spawn-generation response checks remain. The constant overload frame is preserved and is interpreted only as retryable refusal, not authority.

Cancellation stops acceptance, as before. Already spawned handlers are not joined or immediately canceled by this server loop; they retain the original bounded handling timeout. This patch does not introduce or prove transactional rollback of an already dispatched application action.
No native test was executed by this reviewer. Fresh Windows and complete Agentd owner qualification remains with the owner agent. The earlier smaller-library pass cannot replace it.
